title: Filling in the form

fn.en: Ask for clarification when you don’t understand, and complete a form correctly.

useful: Sorry, what do you mean by…?

the day, month and year you were born
the person to call if something happens to you

use: Do you have any places left?
tts: Hello, Action Holidays, Pippa speaking, can I help you? — Yes, I’m interested in going on the scuba-diving course in Thailand, but I’d like to check if it’s suitable for complete beginners.
Yes, that’s not a problem at all. It’s suitable for all levels. When would you like to go? — Well, do you have any places left on one of the January courses?
Just let me check. Yes, the first one’s on the sixth of January. — Sorry, could you say that again? The sixth?
That’s right, the sixth. You’ll need to fill in the registration form online and we’ll send you the joining instructions.

acts.title: Course enrolment form — and what she asked at each line
text: ENROLMENT FORM · Please complete in BLOCK CAPITALS.
SURNAME: SERIKOVA — “Sorry, does surname mean my family name or my first name?”
DATE OF BIRTH: 14 / 06 / 1996 — “Is that day first or month first?” It is day first on this form; on an American form it would not be.
MARITAL STATUS: SINGLE — “What do you mean by marital status?”
OCCUPATION: ENGINEER — “Do I write the job or the company?” The job.
NEXT OF KIN: SERIK SERIKOV (FATHER) — “Sorry, what do you mean by next of kin?” The person to call if something happens to you.
DO YOU HAVE ANY MEDICAL CONDITIONS? YES / NO — “Do I need to fill in this part if the answer is no?” Yes — delete the one that isn’t true, don’t leave it empty.
“One more thing — do I have to sign both pages?” Yes. That is the line most people miss.

write.q: Complete a form for yourself and write down the questions you would ask at each difficult line: 8–10 lines. Use the model’s six moves, and at least three of its phrases: What do you mean by…? / Could you say that again? / Do I need to…? / One more thing… / I’m a bit lost.
write.model: ENROLMENT FORM — complete in BLOCK CAPITALS. SURNAME: ZHAKSYBEK — “Sorry, does surname mean my family name?” FIRST NAME: MARAT. DATE OF BIRTH: 02 / 11 / 1993 — “Is that day first or month first on this form?” MARITAL STATUS: MARRIED. OCCUPATION: TEACHER — “Do I write the job or the school?” NEXT OF KIN: AIGUL ZHAKSYBEK (WIFE) — “What do you mean by next of kin exactly?” DO YOU HAVE ANY MEDICAL CONDITIONS? YES / NO — “Do I need to fill this in if the answer is no?” SIGNATURE: ____ DATE: 12 / 09. “One more thing — do I have to sign both pages?”

speak.q: Play both parts out loud: as the caller, ask three clarification questions about a form; as the office, explain what two of the words mean and what the format is.
